name: Fire-and-rehire / contract-change evidence workflow — conditional test only
demand: The supplied trigger is misattributed: Employment Rights Act 2025 section 25 concerns the unfair-dismissal qualifying period and compensation cap; section 28 covers dismissal for refusing contract variations. SI 2026/559 commences section 25, not the fire-and-rehire protections. The latest GOV.UK timetable, updated 22 October 2026, places those protections in March 2027, while Acas still says January; the GOV.UK timetable says future dates remain subject to parliamentary processes. (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/25/2026-10-01; https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/28; https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/559/made/data.xht?view=snippet&wrap=true; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update; https://www.acas.org.uk/changing-an-employment-contract/employer-responsibilities/if-employment-contract-changes-cannot-be-agreed). The broad UK private-sector pool was 1,417,730 employer businesses at the start of 2025; 266,855 had 10 or more employees, calculated from the published 10–49, 50–249 and 250+ bands. These are population proxies, not likely buyers. (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/business-population-estimates-2025/business-population-estimates-for-the-uk-and-regions-2025-statistical-release). DBT estimates 12,136 employers and 125,000 workers affected annually before the reform, but derived this from an unpublished 2022 YouGov survey and 2024 business estimates; DBT says pandemic-era conditions likely make it an overestimate. ONS’s later survey found fire-and-rehire contract changes too rare to publish. The policy aims to reduce the practice, so neither figure is a forecast of software demand. (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/698370ef20fe1bb69ac24429/fire-and-rehire-options-assessment.pdf). Exact UK search counts, installs, users and product demand are unverified; Google Trends reports sampled, normalized relative interest rather than exact search counts. (https://newsinitiative.withgoogle.com/en-gb/resources/trainings/google-trends/basics-of-google-trends/; https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4355000?hl=en)
prices: Observed asking prices, not verified transactions: HRVANTA’s direct fire-and-rehire PDF toolkit is $20.98 on Etsy; Tarn.hr, an adjacent AI-guided UK HR product, lists £15/month or £150/year; HRDocBox lists a general dismissal toolkit including re-engagement letters for £24.99; ConsultantLM lists fire-and-rehire legal-service stages from £264 to £3,432 in total. Acas also provides free employer advice and a free helpline. The Etsy seller page showed zero shop sales when checked; no realized revenue for this lead or the comparable products is verified. (https://www.etsy.com/listing/4571155465/uk-changing-employment-terms-and-fire?lang_mismatch=1; https://tarn.hr/pricing; https://hrdocbox.co.uk/category.cfm/subcategory/04.09/dismissals-templates-toolkit; https://consultantlm.uk/service/fire-and-rehire-legal-advice; https://www.gov.uk/pay-and-work-rights)
copy_speed: Fast for the basic workflow. A direct 32-page PDF toolkit was listed on Etsy on 8 September 2026; it includes a business-case record, consultation plan and log, decision record, appeal record and post-change review. The listing is a template, not software, and its stated legal timing predates the 22 October government update. ConsultantLM posted a related service page dated 25 August 2026. I found no dated direct fire-and-rehire decision-record SaaS launch; this absence is unverified. Tarn.hr is an adjacent AI HR product at £15/month, but its stated 15 launch situations do not include fire-and-rehire. (https://www.etsy.com/listing/4571155465/uk-changing-employment-terms-and-fire?lang_mismatch=1; https://consultantlm.uk/service/fire-and-rehire-legal-advice; https://tarn.hr/pricing; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update)
platform_risk: High legal-content and substitution risk; moderate technical-platform risk if built as a standalone product. The restricted-variation rules and revised dismissal-and-re-engagement code are still being implemented or consulted on, and official timing currently conflicts between GOV.UK and Acas. Free Acas guidance and helpline support are substitutes; existing HR workflow systems already attach tasks, meetings and documents to employee records. (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/make-work-pay-fire-and-rehire-changes-to-expenses-benefits-and-shift-patterns; https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/make-work-pay-revised-code-of-practice-on-dismissal-and-re-engagement; https://www.acas.org.uk/changing-an-employment-contract/employer-responsibilities/if-employment-contract-changes-cannot-be-agreed; https://www.timeware.co.uk/hrms/workflow). Employee records can include health or union-membership data; ICO guidance requires a lawful basis and, for special-category data, additional conditions. (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/employment/employment-practices-and-data-protection-keeping-employment-records/collecting-and-keeping-employment-records/)
defensible_asset: Potential, not established: a source-linked, versioned GB rules engine plus an auditable record of proposal, alternatives, consultation, responses, approvals and generated documents could save process time and create switching costs as records accumulate. Public law and templates are readily copied; private employee records are a compliance liability, not a reusable data moat. Keep AI to evidence organization, drafting and source-change alerts; require human approval for legal interpretation and employer decisions. (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/28; https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/make-work-pay-revised-code-of-practice-on-dismissal-and-re-engagement; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/employment/employment-practices-and-data-protection-keeping-employment-records/collecting-and-keeping-employment-records/)
build_effort: Estimated, unverified: a no-code demo is small; production software is a multi-week build for secure employer accounts, a versioned rules table, consultation timelines, evidence logs, document export, access controls, retention/deletion and billing. AI agents could handle intake, document assembly, reminders, billing support and draft monitoring of official sources. Human legal review of rule changes and exception cases remains necessary. Similar AI-guided HR document generation is offered by Tarn.hr, but no source verifies its automation share or operator hours. (https://tarn.hr/pricing; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/employment/employment-practices-and-data-protection-keeping-employment-records/collecting-and-keeping-employment-records/)
channel: Prefer inbound search content under a product brand, a free source-linked contract-change checklist, opt-in updates and referrals through employment-law, payroll or HR advisers. No face or personal brand is required. Do not rely on cold messages to individuals or sole traders: ICO says PECR treats sole traders and some partnerships like individuals, and its electronic-mail rules also cover texts and social-media direct messages; direct marketing to them generally needs consent or a valid soft opt-in. (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified target: 3–5 hours/week at steady state, excluding the initial build and any external legal-review work. There is no operating product or workload evidence to show this ceiling is achievable; exception-heavy support or frequent law changes could exceed it.
desk_test: One workday, no employee data: make a clickable consultation-record demo and one sample export from the current official Acas/GOV.UK process; publish a product-branded page with a clear £15/month pilot price, using Tarn.hr’s observed price as the test anchor, and a refundable paid-reservation option. Share it once in a moderator-approved HR community or through an opt-in adviser channel; count payment intent only when an employing company or HR adviser reserves, not from likes or downloads. If no reservation, stop before production build. (https://tarn.hr/pricing; https://www.acas.org.uk/changing-an-employment-contract/employer-responsibilities/if-employment-contract-changes-cannot-be-agreed; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)
red_flags: Conditional survive for a desk test, not a production build. The supplied January trigger was tied to the wrong section; the newest GOV.UK timetable says March 2027 while Acas still says January. The underlying practice is rare, the government intends to reduce it, exact search demand is unverified, one direct low-cost template competitor already exists, observed prices are low, and no realized revenue or customer demand is verified. The 55% automation figure and ≤5-hour operating target are planning assumptions, not measured results. Do not imply that a completed record makes a dismissal lawful. (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/25/2026-10-01; https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/28; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update; https://www.acas.org.uk/changing-an-employment-contract/employer-responsibilities/if-employment-contract-changes-cannot-be-agreed; https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/698370ef20fe1bb69ac24429/fire-and-rehire-options-assessment.pdf; https://www.etsy.com/listing/4571155465/uk-changing-employment-terms-and-fire?lang_mismatch=1)
